name: ifconfig
description: The classic interface configuration tool from net-tools. Still present for compatibility, superseded by ip.

flags.description: Show active interfaces with addresses and statistics.
Enable or disable an interface (deprecated syntax).

examples.output:
eth0: flags=4163<UP,BROADCAST,RUNNING,MULTICAST> mtu 1500
      inet 192.168.1.20  netmask 255.255.255.0
      RX packets 104231  bytes 128443012 (122.4 MiB)
examples.explanation: Shows interface state, IPv4 address, netmask, and RX/TX packet counters.
Also lists interfaces that are currently down.

about: net-tools (ifconfig, route, netstat) has not tracked modern kernel features for years: it hides secondary addresses, cannot show policy routing, and its output format is fixed. Linux distributions keep it only for habit and old scripts — new work should use ip.
useCases: Quick familiar checks on older servers.
mistakes: Using ifconfig in new scripts — prefer ip.
Expecting it to be installed by default: many minimal images omit net-tools entirely.
warnings: Deprecated. Modern distributions may not include it at all.
distroNotes: Available via the net-tools package (optional on Debian/Ubuntu and Fedora; not installed by default on many minimal images).
